pages.title: File:N8042W Convair CV-440-75- Museo Aeronáutico de Málaga 2.2.24 (53514183467).jpg

ObjectName.value: N8042W Convair CV-440-75- Museo Aeronáutico de Málaga 2.2.24 (53514183467)

Categories.value: Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Photographs by Colin Cooke

ImageDescription.value:
This delightful small aviation museum exists in the old terminal building and surrounds at Malaga Airport. Not a many actual aircraft but these two propliners are in good condition despite not wearing original paint schemes.

Though painted as OH-VKN, this aircraft didn't actually serve with Kar-Air. However it did fly for many years in Scandinavia, having been delivered to SAS as SE-BSY in February 1958. After being sold in the mid-1970s it went on to fly in Botswana and South Africa before being acquired by Cochise Airlines in 1979. After being parked at Malaga for some years, the airport acquired the aircraft, repainted it and put it on display.

Credit.value: N8042W Convair CV-440-75- Museo Aeronáutico de Málaga 2.2.24

pages.title: File:EC-CPO Douglas C-47B Skytrain Museo Aeronáutico de Málaga 2.2.24 (53515503635).jpg

ObjectName.value: EC-CPO Douglas C-47B Skytrain Museo Aeronáutico de Málaga 2.2.24 (53515503635)

Categories.value: Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Photographs by Colin Cooke

ImageDescription.value:
This delightful small aviation museum exists in the old terminal building and surrounds at Malaga Airport. Not a many actual aircraft but these two propliners are in good condition despite not wearing original paint schemes.

Delivered to the USAAF as 45-1091 in 1945. Registered as N86442 then to the Spanish Air Force as T.3-50 in 1962. To Aerotransporte de España as EC-CPO in 1978. Stored at Zaragoza by 1992. Moved to Malaga in 2003 and preserved at the Museum as EC-ABC.

The original EC-ABC belong to Iberia, but crashed on Wednesday 29 April 1959. The DC-3 departed Barcelona at 14:18 GMT for a flight to Madrid. A severe storm over Calamocha forced the crew to fly another course. Shortly after having been in contact with Calamocha, the plane crashed on the east slope of the Sierra de Valdemeca, some 60 m from the top of Telegraph Hill.

Credit.value: EC-CPO Douglas C-47B Skytrain Museo Aeronáutico de Málaga 2.2.24
